verses.text: “Then the Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.
Five were foolish, and five were wise.
The foolish ones took their lamps but didn’t bring extra oil.
The wise ones brought oil in jars along with their lamps.
The groom took a long time coming, so they all got drowsy and fell asleep.
At midnight someone shouted, ‘Look! The groom is coming! Come out to meet him!’
Then all the young women woke up and prepared their lamps.
The foolish ones said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil. Our lamps are going out.’
The wise ones replied, ‘There may not be enough for all of us. Go to the sellers and buy some for yourselves.’
While they were away buying oil, the groom arrived. The ones who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
Later, the other young women came and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us!’
But he answered, ‘I’m telling you the truth: I don’t know you.’
So stay alert, because you don’t know the day or the hour the Son of Man is coming.
“It’s like a man who was going on a journey. He called his servants and entrusted his property to them.
He gave five talents to one, two to another, and one to a third—each according to their ability. Then he left on his journey.
The servant who received five talents went and traded with them, earning five more.
In the same way, the one who received two talents earned two more.
But the servant who received one talent went and dug a hole in the ground and hid his master’s money.
“After a long time, the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.
The servant who had received five talents brought the extra five and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with five talents. Look, I’ve earned five more.’
His master said, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful with a few things, so I’ll put you in charge of many things. Come share your master’s joy.’
“The servant who had received two talents came and said, ‘Master, you entrusted me with two talents. Look, I’ve earned two more.’
His master told him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant! You were faithful with a few things, so I’ll put you in charge of many things. Come share your master’s joy.’
“Then the servant who had received one talent came and said, ‘Master, I knew you’re a harsh man. You harvest where you didn’t plant and gather where you didn’t scatter.
I was afraid, so I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you can have back what belongs to you.’
“His master answered, ‘You wicked, lazy servant! You knew I harvest where I didn’t plant and gather where I didn’t scatter.
Then you should have deposited my money with the bankers. When I returned, I could have collected it with interest.
Take the talent from him and give it to the one who has ten.
Everyone who has will be given more, and they’ll have plenty. But from the one who has nothing, even what they have will be taken away.
Throw that useless servant into the darkness outside, where people weep and grind their teeth.’
“When the Son of Man comes in his glory with all the holy angels, he’ll sit on his glorious throne.
All the nations will be gathered in front of him. He’ll separate people from one another, like a shepherd separates sheep from goats.
He’ll put the sheep at his right and the goats at his left.
Then the King will say to those at his right, ‘Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Inherit the Kingdom prepared for you since the world began.
I was hungry, and you gave me food. I was thirsty, and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed me.
I had no clothes, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you cared for me. I was in prison, and you visited me.’
“Then the righteous will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?
When did we see you as a stranger and welcome you, or without clothes and clothe you?
When did we see you sick or in prison and visit you?’
“The King will answer, ‘I’m telling you the truth: whatever you did for one of the least of these my brothers and sisters, you did for me.’
Then he’ll say to those at his left, ‘Get away from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
I was hungry, and you gave me no food. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink.
I was a stranger, and you didn’t welcome me. I had no clothes, and you didn’t clothe me. I was sick and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’
“Then they’ll answer, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, thirsty, a stranger, without clothes, sick, or in prison and fail to help you?’
“He’ll answer them, ‘I’m telling you the truth: whatever you failed to do for one of the least of these, you failed to do for me.’
They’ll go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous will enter eternal life.”
